land.text: 'On 18 April 1980, Zimbabwe Rhodesia became the independent Republic of Zimbabwe within the Commonwealth of Nations' (Zimbabwe Rhodesia page); the Zimbabwe page has 'On 11 April 1980, Southern Rhodesia became the independent nation of Zimbabwe'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Zimbabwe Rhodesia row (1979-1982, same outline, 392,765 km2) covers the first three years of this state; its 'Republic of Zimbabwe' row begins in 1983. The Zimbabwe Rhodesia page gives that state's life as 1 June 1979 to 18 April 1980, with a reversion to British rule as Southern Rhodesia on 11-12 December 1979.

capitals.name: Salisbury (Harare)
capitals.note: Salisbury renamed Harare: the Zimbabwe page says the new place names were 'gazetted on 18 April 1982' and lists 'Salisbury/Harare' among the colonial names changed; it gives no separate date for the capital's own renaming.

rulers.name: Robert Mugabe
rulers.title: head of government from 1980; executive president after the 1987 constitutional revision
rulers.note: The Zimbabwe page: 'Mugabe and the ZANU party secured a landslide victory' in the 1980 election; 'In 1987, Mugabe revised the constitution, abolishing the ceremonial presidency'; 'On 21 November 2017, Mugabe tendered his resignation prior to impeachment proceedings being completed.' The page names neither the office Mugabe took in 1980 nor a start-of-office date.

rulers.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'Emmerson Mnangagwa was appointed president following this coup'; re-elected August 2023 per the page.

correction.text: the territory of Zimbabwe Rhodesia, which 'became the independent Republic of Zimbabwe' on 18 April 1980: the shape is Cliopatria's Zimbabwe Rhodesia outline, unchanged, drawn as this state

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria starts the Republic of Zimbabwe in 1983 and labels 1979-1982 'Zimbabwe Rhodesia', but the Zimbabwe Rhodesia page ends that state on 18 April 1980 (body text) or 11-12 December 1979 (infobox 'British-supervised transition: 11-12 December 1979', reversion to British rule) and the Zimbabwe page has independence in April 1980. Same 392,765 km2 outline, so only the owner of 1980-1982 changes; the Zimbabwe Rhodesia dossier (another group) should end in 1980.

392,765 km2 against the infobox 'Total area 390,757 km2' (ratio 1.005). The page records no border change after independence and no border dispute, so the one outline stands to 2023. The shape's modern_countries column also lists Botswana and Zambia: those are most likely rim cells of the rasterised outline, not territory (the page records no land held outside the country).
Identical to the 1983 shape; nothing on the page changes the state's land in 2024.

region.text: Southern Rhodesia, 'the independent nation of Zimbabwe'

ledger.note: 1980: Zimbabwe becomes independent under Mugabe. 'On 18 April 1980, Zimbabwe Rhodesia became the independent Republic of Zimbabwe within the Commonwealth of Nations' (Zimbabwe Rhodesia page; infobox 'Independence recognised: 18 April 1980' on the Zimbabwe page, whose body text reads 'On 11 April 1980, Southern Rhodesia became the independent nation of Zimbabwe'). The pages give the state, not a boundary; the land is Cliopatria's outline.

wars.name: Second Congo War
wars.outcome: No territorial result for Zimbabwe: the page records only 'Zimbabwe's involvement from 1998 to 2002 in the war in the Democratic Republic of the Congo' and its cost to the economy.
wars.note: The page does not say on which side Zimbabwe fought or name the other belligerents; the Congo war's own dossier owns the zones.

wars.name: Gukurahundi (Matabeleland unrest)
wars.outcome: Internal campaign by the Fifth Brigade in Matabeleland, with no change of border; 'The campaign officially ended in 1987 after Nkomo and Mugabe reached a unity agreement'.
wars.note: 'The Fifth Brigade was formed in 1981 and disbanded in 1988'; the page gives no start year for the campaign.

certainty.note: The Zimbabwe page records no border dispute or border change after independence; no page opened gives treaty text, so the level rests on that silence.

sources.title: Zimbabwe Rhodesia
sources.note: The 1979-1980 sequence behind the transition from Southern Rhodesia to Zimbabwe, and why Cliopatria's 1979-1982 row is a different name for the same outline.

notes: Page budget 1-2: two pages opened. (1) Cliopatria begins the Republic of Zimbabwe in 1983, three years after independence; the row 'Zimbabwe Rhodesia' (slug zimbabwe-rhodesia, 1979-1982) carries the same 392,765 km2 outline. This dossier therefore starts in April 1980 with a new keyframe for 1980-1982; the zimbabwe-rhodesia dossier (another group) should end in 1980 (the pages give 11-12 December 1979 for the reversion to British rule and 18 April 1980 for independence) and hand over to this state. (2) The two pages disagree on the independence date: Zimbabwe infobox 18 April 1980, Zimbabwe body text 11 April 1980, Zimbabwe Rhodesia page 18 April 1980; the dossier uses April 1980 and 18 April. (3) Neither page was read for the Rhodesian Bush War or the 1980s border incidents with Mozambique and Zambia; the Zimbabwe page has none, and no border change is recorded. (4) No gazetteer names are missing: only the Cliopatria reference is used.
